name: Raw Browser
description: Drives the Chrome or Edge you are already signed into: 16 tools for tabs, navigation, reading, clicking, filling, screenshots and cookies. Read-only tools inherit normal policy; navigation and input are reviewed; raw_screenshot is reviewed because it writes a PNG; raw_visit, raw_cookies, raw_eval and raw_call are blocked. On Windows, install with npm install -g raw-browser, run the bridge installer, and load its unpacked extension with Developer mode before starting raw-mcp. Off until you turn it on.
saferAlternatives: Prefer raw_status, raw_tabs, raw_text, raw_html, raw_snapshot and raw_frames; they read the current tab without changing it.
raw_screenshot also reads the tab, but it writes a PNG to the working directory or the caller's out path. Review it before approving and point it at a dedicated output directory.
raw_eval, raw_visit and raw_call are blocked: raw_eval and raw_visit run arbitrary page JavaScript, and raw_call can invoke any Raw.* / CDP method. Use the typed tool that performs the same action.
raw_cookies is blocked because it returns live session cookie values. Use a browser profile dedicated to the agent and keep cookie values out of model context.
raw_click, raw_fill, raw_goto and raw_new can submit forms, start purchases, or carry data in a URL. Read every argument before approving.
The bridge listens only on 127.0.0.1 and requires the per-browser token; keep the token local and do not expose the port.
